text:
Sunshine all morning and it's already in the low 40s, so the day is playing out as the forecasters expected: bright, dry and chilly. We should creep up to about 46 this afternoon, a touch cooler than a typical late October day, but the breeze is light enough that the sun does most of the talking. A jacket and a hat will be plenty for a lunchtime walk or the ride home.

The sun sets around 5:50, and with the air this dry, the temperature will drop quickly after that. Expect a clear, cold night with a low around 26, so frost on the windshield and a hard freeze for anything tender still outside.

Wednesday starts frosty, then clouds fill in through the morning and we climb to about 53. It stays dry. Thursday turns noticeably milder, with highs in the low to mid 60s. Light showers arrive Thursday night into Friday morning, but the amounts look tiny. I'd bring in the plants tonight and leave the umbrella at home.

AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-10-27T11:20:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. Cold weather for today will be followed by gradually warming conditions ahead of a weak front with light rain late Thursday into Friday.
  2. Dry and seasonable weather is expected over the weekend, with increased chances for showers early next week.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 223 AM EDT Tuesday... No notable changes have been made to the forecast.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: Another cool day is expected as a seasonably chilly air mass remains overhead. Temperatures will linger in the 40s for most, with a few 50s in the Upper Valley. The air mass is also dry, and mountain summits will feel especially crisp with dewpoints in the single digits in Fahrenheit heading below 0. Closer to the ground, another day with relative humidity values ranging in the 30s, locally down into the upper 20 percent range, is expected. Fortunately, winds stay relatively light in the afternoon, but a few gusts to 15 mph are possible across Vermont. Dry air will result in a chilly night in the teens to mid 20s tonight. The only thing preventing prime radiational cooling will be some incoming high clouds in northern New York. Nevertheless, a few climate sites will be in striking distance of record lows. High pressure will amble offshore Wednesday, and more seasonable temperatures are expected. A passing mid-level trough will slide east, and with it will be some increasing clouds. Low-level conditions will be much too dry for any precipitation to approach the surface. Surface relative humidity values will be about the same with light winds switching to the south midday. Forecast weather for Thursday will be warmer with high temperatures climbing into the 60s, but that will come with the price of increasing south to southwesterly gusts west of the Greens into northern New York of 20-30 mph. This will signal an incoming cold front, approaching the St. Lawrence Valley by Thursday evening. The tongue of moisture along the front is fairly narrow, and the synoptic forcing is not anything noteworthy, but they should be enough to produce light rain. It will be in the process of decay, though. So it is likely to produce more precipitation across northern areas than in south-central Vermont. Mainly a few hundredths up to a tenth is expected, mainly along northwest slopes of the northern Greens/northern Adirondacks and along the international border. A few showers will linger across northern mountains Friday afternoon, but trending dry gain into the weekend. KEY MESSAGE 2: In the wake of a frontal boundary moving through the region late this week, high pressure looks to build over the region for the weekend, bringing another period of dry and seasonable weather. High temperatures will generally climb into the 50s and low 60s this weekend. Heading into the start of next week, there looks to be increasing chance for showers and an end to our dry weather pattern, although there is still a lot of uncertainty amongst models and the overall pattern evolution at this time.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) -Happy Tuesday! After a cloudier day north yesterday, Tuesday features more sunshine for all of us, but we do turn a bit cooler, with most climbing into the 40s this afternoon for most. Southern Vermont could be a tad warmer in the low to mid 50s for Tuesday afternoon. A cool day is followed by a cool night and most fall back into the teens and 20s for early Wednesday morning. After a cool start Wednesday morning, more cloud cover begins to fill in through the morning hours Wednesday leaving us a gray and cloudier into Wednesday afternoon. Temperatures are a tad warmer though, as we climb towards the upper 40s and 50s for afternoon highs. Thursday we look to be even warmer as most climb towards the low to mid 60s for Thursday afternoon. A few clouds may begin to build in through the day Thursday, and could give way to a few showers Thursday evening into Thursday night. Any rain should be wrapping up by Friday morning, but we may hang onto a bit more cloud cover especially through the first half of the day Friday with high temperatures in the upper 50s to lower 60s. The weekend forecast at this point is not looking too bad. Saturday for Halloween features nice sunshine with temperatures into the 50s. Trick-Or-Treat time remains clear as temperatures dip into the 40s and lower 50s. Don’t forget we fall back 1 hour Saturday night into Sunday. Sunday features more sunshine with high temperatures in the 50s. There is the chance for maybe a few hit-or-miss showers into the day Monday with temperatures again in the 50s to about 60 for Monday afternoon.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-10-26T21:40:00Z — same caveat): Cold but bright Tuesday — Tuesday will feature nearly full sunshine, as high pressure builds in, but it will be unseasonably cool. Highs only reach the mid to upper 40s, with a noticeable north breeze. Wednesday starts with another widespread freeze. A warm front brings a band of clouds in the morning, giving way to more afternoon sun. Highs rebound to the mid-50s. Thursday turns quite mild, as a gusty south breeze sends highs to around 70. After a sunny start, clouds increase through the afternoon. Another cold front brings a few showers Thursday night, though not expecting significant rain. A couple showers linger early Friday, otherwise expecting a nice day with a mix of sun and clouds. Highs will be near 60. Halloween weekend starts bright but cool on Saturday, with highs near 50. A few more clouds are likely Sunday, though it stays mostly dry and turns milder. Highs will be near 60.
